scope_note: V-FINAL adversarial audit of the shipping bytes of batches/batch18/candidates/las-b18-002.json (LAS debatt short, family elljusspar-slackning-debatt-short, 2 questions, keys C/B) after fleet-repair-2 (Q1-B off the calendar), fleet-repair-3 (Q1 stem bound to ”besparingskalkyl”, Q1-A and Q1-D rebuilt in the overstatement direction) and fleet-repair-3b (G-SPRÅK r3 rationale scrub). Prime directive was to REFUTE: to make Q1-B (”Den bygger på en enda räkning av löpare”) defensible against the tightened stem, to break the new Q1-A and Q1-D, to falsify the declared blind floors (Q1 1-in-3, Q2 1-in-2), to falsify the repair_log against the bytes, and to re-run law 16 rather than re-read it. The keys did not fall. B, A and D are each refutable from the passage alone. What did fall: one clause of Swedish that fleet-repair-3b broke while claiming to have applied the gate's own native alternative, the recorded derivations of BOTH declared blind floors, two accuracy items in the originality_note (one of them a RULE 14 gap this audit closed by probing the missing one-diacritic variant), a self-contradiction inside the Q1 rationale, and the state of M-FORM's absolutizer list in this worktree.
severity_contract: findings[].severity is drawn ONLY from {minor, note, info}. A ship-blocker is expressed as verdict REFUTED, never as a custom severity. Nothing found here rises to REFUTED: both keys are correct and uniquely text-supported, both survive an argue-every-option re-derivation, all six mech gates re-run pass on the shipping bytes, every rationale quotation resolves, the arithmetic reconciles exactly, the three derived sheets are exact leak-free projections, and law 16 reproduces clean with passing positive controls on both endpoints. The findings are one repair-introduced grammar defect, two falsified floor derivations, one rationale self-contradiction, one carried 3-of-3 G-SPRÅK minor on a student-facing option, one cosmetic calendar gap, two search-log accuracy items and two process/registry items.

cold_solve.method_honesty: DISCLOSED LIMIT. The tasking required reading the candidate in FULL first, keys and rationales included, so no genuinely key-blind first solve was available to this audit. What is recorded below is therefore two separate exercises, kept apart: (1) a PASSAGE RE-DERIVATION in which every option was argued FOR to a textual verdict before any option was rejected, and (2) a BLIND RECONSTRUCTION performed against stems/las-b18-002.json alone (no passage, no title, no key, no rationale), asking only where the form and the cross-question structure carry a solver. The second is what bears on the floors; it is stated as a reconstruction, not as a virgin solve.

passage_rederivation.q1: C. Argued FOR A (”Den räknar med för många armaturer i stolparna”): the passage hands A its own words — ”Räknar man i stället på de armaturer som faktiskt sitter i stolparna” — and ”faktiskt sitter” can on a fast read be taken as a contrast of NUMBER (fixtures really up there vs fixtures assumed). REJECTED: the two sentences immediately before fix the contrast as a contrast of SORT — ”Vintern 2023 byttes spårets gamla kvicksilverlampor mot ledbelysning” and ”Kalkylen utgår ändå från de gamla lamporna” — and no count of armaturer appears anywhere in the passage. The one armatur the passage does single out sits elsewhere by name: ”den har en egen liten armatur”, in the monter, not i stolparna. Argued FOR B (”Den bygger på en enda räkning av löpare”), the strongest residual and the one the counsel history names: the author really does attack a single count — ”som stöd redovisas ett besök i augusti då förvaltningen räknade till fyra personer på spåret efter nio” and ”Augustibesöket bevisar inte heller det som tjänsteskrivelsen låter påskina” — and the count sits INSIDE the paragraph that opens ”Siffran 38 000 tål en närmare titt”, with an ”inte HELLER” that rhetorically chains it to the lamp argument. That is the best case and it fails twice. (i) The passage assigns the count a different target in the sentence that introduces it: ”Ingreppet beskrivs som ”begränsat för flertalet motionärer”, och som stöd redovisas ett besök i augusti” — stöd for the IMPACT claim, not for the money. (ii) The author's rebuttal of the count is about darkness and need, not about kronor: ”I augusti är det ljust till halv tio”, ”De mörka kvällstimmarna infaller mellan oktober och mars”. With the stem bound to ”besparingskalkyl”, B's ”Den” resolves to the 38 000-kronor computation, and an attendance figure is not an input to it. B is defeated — but it remains the unit's strongest distractor and the defeat runs through the stem's noun, exactly as G-DISTRACTOR r2 predicted and r3 recorded. Argued FOR D (”Den räknar med fler timmar än beslutet gäller”): an inflated hour count would inflate the saving, so the direction is right, and the author's summer concession (”då gör belysningen ingen nytta”) can be strained into ”hours that should not have been counted”. REJECTED: the decision is two hours on its face — ”spåret släcks klockan 21 i stället för klockan 23” — and the author's own recomputation starts from the same ”två kvällstimmar”; and the strained reading attacks his own concession, since switching off useless summer light is a real saving he grants. C is the only option the passage licenses: ”Kalkylen utgår ändå från de gamla lamporna” is exactly ”räknar på lampor som redan är utbytta”, paraphrased, with no verbatim lift.
passage_rederivation.q2: B. Argued FOR A (”Belysningen bör lysa till klockan 23 året om”): the author's whole grievance is the lost 21–23 window and he does demand ”håll tänt till elva”. REJECTED by one clause — ”Släck vid nio på sommaren” in his own proposal, and ”mellan maj och augusti kan spåret gott släckas tidigt” before it. Argued FOR C (”Besparingen är visserligen betydande men hämtas i fel verksamhet”): the second conjunct is close to his position, and his gravel-delivery comparison (”ungefär vad en enda grusleverans till spåret gick på i våras”) is a budget-scale argument of that family. REJECTED on the first conjunct, which reverses his central number: he puts the real saving at ”omkring tolv tusen kronor om året” against the tjänsteskrivelse's 38 000. Argued FOR D: the passage does concede the cost pressure, ”Elnotan har stigit” and ”Spartrycket är verkligt”. REJECTED by the entire closing move, ”Gör därför om beslutet i stället för att försvara det”. B spans both halves of §5 and is uniquely correct.
passage_rederivation.agrees_with_gkey_legs: Yes, and with every leg on record: six G-KEY legs across three rounds (verdicts-gkey-1/-2, -r2-1/-r2-2, -r3-1/-r3-2) all return C and B, 0 kills, 0 flags, each citing the same two anchor sentences this audit reached.

blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.input: stems/las-b18-002.json — two prompts and eight option strings. No passage, no title, no key, no rationale, no generator_meta (verified: the sheet carries only candidate_id, section, questions).
blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.q1_lands_on: C, for a form-sensitive solver; genuinely open among three for a plain one.
blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.q1_path: Strip B first: it is the odd option on the verb (”Den bygger på” against three ”Den räknar”) and, semantically, a headcount is not a line in a kronor computation — this strip is the one the generator itself prices into the 1-in-3 floor. That leaves A, C, D, which the repair_log calls ”tre likriktade angrepp … med identisk form”. The form is NOT identical. A and D are syntactic twins, ”Den räknar MED” plus a comparative-quantity phrase (”för många armaturer i stolparna” / ”fler timmar än beslutet gäller”); C is a different frame, ”Den räknar PÅ” plus a basis (”lampor som redan är utbytta”). Two formally parallel co-hyponyms that differ only in which input they name give a test-wise solver the symmetric-pair elimination: neither twin has an edge over the other, so an item with one key is unlikely to have made either of them the key. Strip both, land on C.
blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.q2_lands_on: B, for a solver who works Q2 after reading Q1's stem and applies the maximalist strip.
blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.q2_path: Three strips, each independently attested in this unit's own record. (1) D dies on Q1's stem, which asserts as fact that the author points to a weakness in the municipality's SAVINGS calculation — an author doing that is not the author of ”Motionärer får tåla sämre service”. G-STEM r3 records exactly this at major severity: ”a cross-question direction-of-argument leak”. (2) C dies on the same stem, one step further: an author who says the savings figure is wrong will not concede it is ”visserligen betydande”. The generator concedes this strip in its own RULE 12 table — ”skärpningen ”besparings-” gör dessutom Q2-C:s ”visserligen betydande” mindre trolig” — and even names the lexical vehicle, the shared 5-character stem bespa- between the stem's ”besparingskalkyl” and C's ”Besparingen”. (3) A dies on form: ”året om” is the set's one maximalist. G-STEM r3 performed precisely this strip — ”An absolutizer strip removes this maximalist year-round demand”. What remains is B alone, the key.
blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.empirical_counterweight: Recorded because it cuts against the reconstruction and must not be suppressed. G-STEM r3, holding both stems and both option sets and no passage, returned PASS on q:1 — it did not find Q1 solvable at all — and on q:2 it recorded ”blind pick C”, i.e. it made strips (1) and (3) but NOT strip (2), and then chose the wrong option of the surviving pair on the concessive-shape heuristic. So the chains above are heuristic, not deterministic, and the one live blind reader on record missed Q2 rather than hitting it. That is why both floor findings are recorded at minor/note and neither is a blocker.

floors_assessment.q1_honest: HONEST AS A NUMBER FOR A PLAIN SOLVER, OPTIMISTIC FOR A FORM-SENSITIVE ONE (~1-in-2). The claim that fleet-repair-3 removed the blind strike on A and D is true for the ground it removed — the pre-repair A and D really did make the saving LARGER and really were self-defeating as ”svagheter”, and that channel is closed. But the repair replaced a direction twinning with a SYNTAX twinning: A and D now share a frame that C does not, and the repair_log's own justification for the new floor (”identisk form och 8 ord var”) is half false on the bytes. The word half is exact and this audit re-derived it: A 8 / B 8 / C 8 / D 8, ratio 1.00. The form half is not.
floors_assessment.q2_honest: AT THE CEILING, NOT BELOW IT. The NUMBER survives; the recorded DERIVATION does not. The generator's derivation strips D and C and then calls the residual pair {A, B} ”ett ärligt myntkast” on the ground that ”enhetens hedgekorrelation är bruten (Q1-nyckeln är platt)”. That ground is about the UNIT, and the choice is inside Q2. Q2's hedge balance was bought by C also being hedged (”visserligen”) — hedge_map says so — and C is precisely what the same stem strips. In the residual pair the key B is the sole qualified option and A carries the set's one maximalist, so the third strip is available and G-STEM r3 performed it. Honest floor: at 1-in-2 for a solver who takes two of the three strips, and a single survivor for one who takes all three.

stance_policy_compliance.policy: BRIEF-ADDENDUM efterhandstillägg 1 (ägardom batch16 dom 1): cross-question stance correlation is REPORTABLE at note severity and does not block, PROVIDED (a) the adversarial blind floor is stated explicitly and is no better than 1-in-2, and (b) rule 10 holds.
stance_policy_compliance.condition_b: HOLDS, verified rather than accepted. ”Choose the qualified” is inert on Q1 (after fleet-repair-3 no Q1 option is hedged — the pre-repair A ”kan vara” left with the option that carried it) and hits the key on Q2, so 1 of 2, not more than half. Rule 13's stricter form also holds on the full sets: Q2 has TWO qualified options (B ”kan godtas … men bör” and C ”visserligen … men”), not exactly one. Independently verified against the live gate source: no option in the unit carries a mech._ABSOLUTIZERS token (scan run by this audit against the imported set, 8/8 clean).
stance_policy_compliance.condition_a: MET, THINLY. The floor is stated explicitly, in two places (generator_meta and NOTES), and the stated number is 1-in-2, which is the tolerated maximum rather than better than it. What this audit refutes is the reasoning behind the number, not the number: the declared residual pair is wrong and the declared reason it is a coin flip does not apply to that pair. The compliance therefore rests on a number whose support is unsound, and rule 13's protection on Q2 is nullified by the very strip the policy contemplates.
stance_policy_compliance.ruling: COMPLIANT, RECORDED, NOT BLOCKING — consistent with the standing precedent in batches/batch16/audits/las-b16-002.json (stance_channel_ruling: TOLERABLE, no repair, recorded at note). The owner may wish to buy the margin back, because it is cheap. Two candidate edits, neither touching the passage, the keys, the key letters or Q1: (i) take the maximalist off Q2-A so the form strip is unavailable, e.g. ”Belysningen bör lysa till klockan 23 som förr.” — 8 words, ratio unchanged, trap unchanged (overgeneralisation past the summer concession), no month or season token, no new cross-question bridge; or (ii) the edit that actually restores the balance, re-cut Q2-C so Q1's stem no longer strips it, by dropping the ”betydande” that reverses the author's number while keeping the ”fel verksamhet” half. (ii) is the stronger of the two because it puts a second qualified option back into the residual set rather than merely removing a tell from A.

findings.claim: fleet-repair-3b broke a clause of Swedish in the Q1 teaching payload while its own repair_log records the round as having applied ”native alternatives per G-SPRÅK r3”. The shipping sentence is worse than the defect it was repairing.
findings.evidence: G-SPRÅK r3 run 2 flagged, at MINOR, the pre-3b string ”en räkning av personer är över huvud taget ingen post i en kronbesparing” (class 1/6, nonce compound: kron- denotes the coin or the currency, so ”saving expressed in kronor” does not come out), and prescribed the native alternative ”ingen post i en besparing räknad i kronor”. The shipping bytes read: ”… och en räkning av personer är över huvud taget ingen post i en kronor i besparing.” That is neither the prescription nor grammatical Swedish: ”en kronor” puts a singular common-gender article on a plural noun, and ”en kronor i besparing” is not a Swedish nominal at all — the words of the prescribed phrase have been transposed. For contrast, the round's other two named edits were executed to the letter: ”Stammen säger efter fleet-repair-3 uttryckligen ”besparingskalkyl”” → ”Stammen säger uttryckligen ”besparingskalkyl”” and ”men texten strider aldrig om HUR MÅNGA armaturer som sitter uppe, utan om VILKA” → ”men textens invändning gäller aldrig hur många armaturer som sitter uppe, utan vilka”, both character for character as the gate wrote them. Verified absent from student-facing text and present only in generator_meta bookkeeping: ”fleet-repair”, ”strider aldrig om”, ”kronbesparing”, and the all-caps emphasis is gone entirely.
findings.why: This is the one objective defect in the unit. It is not a style preference a copy editor might or might not take — the phrase does not parse, in the Swedish explanation payload of a Swedish-exam trainer, in the very clause that carries the argument defeating the unit's strongest distractor. Severity is minor rather than a refutation because it is one clause, it moves no key, it makes no distractor defensible and the argument survives its own wording. But it should not ship: the fix is a one-clause substitution of the gate's own prescription, ”… är över huvud taget ingen post i en besparing räknad i kronor”, with no effect on any option, stem, passage, key or length. The secondary point is a record point: a repair round that logs ”native alternatives per G-SPRÅK r3” and delivers a worse string than the gate flagged is a repair the ledger cannot be read on trust.

findings.claim: Q2's declared blind floor of 1-in-2 is stated with a derivation that does not survive its own strips. The declared residual pair is wrong, and the reason given for calling that pair a coin flip is about the unit rather than about the pair. Three independently attested strips compose to leave the key alone.
findings.evidence: generator_meta.adversarial_blind_floors[”2”]: ”en stance-van lösare stryker D … och misstror C:s beröm av besparingens storlek; mellan A … och B … avgör inget utanför passagen”, and NOTES: ”enhetens hedgekorrelation är bruten (Q1-nyckeln är platt), så valet A/B är ett ärligt myntkast”. Both strips are conceded in the generator's own RULE 12 table, C explicitly — ”skärpningen ”besparings-” gör dessutom Q2-C:s ”visserligen betydande” mindre trolig” — together with the lexical vehicle, the shared 5-character stem bespa- between the Q1 stem and Q2-C. But hedge_map states that Q2's rule-13 protection IS C: ”nyckeln B är den villkorade … och distraktor C är också hedgad (”visserligen”)”. Strip C and the protection goes with it: in {A, B} the key B is the sole qualified option (”kan godtas … men bör”) and A carries the set's one maximalist (”året om”). The third strip is not this audit's invention — G-STEM r3 performed it on the record: ”An absolutizer strip removes this maximalist year-round demand”, filed at major alongside ”a cross-question direction-of-argument leak”. Composed: D by direction, C by the same stem, A by form; survivor B, the key.
findings.why: The tasking asked whether the adopted stance policy's tolerance is earned. Its condition is that the floor be stated explicitly AND be no better than 1-in-2. It is stated, twice, and the number is the tolerated maximum — so the letter is met. What fails is the support: rule 13's balance on Q2 was purchased with the very option the cross-question strip removes, so the unit's protection and its leak are the same object seen twice. Recorded at minor, not as a refutation, on three grounds. (i) The severity contract reserves refutation for blockers, and nothing here touches key correctness — six G-KEY legs and this audit's re-derivation all reach B on ”för sommaren har nämnden faktiskt en poäng” plus ”håll tänt till elva från oktober till mars”, and B is uniquely licensed. (ii) The chain is heuristic: the one live blind reader on record, G-STEM r3 with both stems in hand, took strips (1) and (3) but not (2) and picked C — it MISSED. (iii) There is standing precedent, batches/batch16/audits/las-b16-002.json, ruling an equivalent cross-question stance channel TOLERABLE at note with written reasoning. The margin is nonetheless cheap to buy back, and the stronger of the two candidate edits is to re-cut Q2-C so the Q1 stem no longer strips it — dropping the ”betydande” that reverses the author's own number while keeping the ”fel verksamhet” half — which puts a second qualified option back into the residual set instead of merely removing a tell from A. See floors_assessment.stance_policy_compliance for the full ruling.

findings.claim: Q1's floor really did improve from 1-in-2 to something looser — the direction defect fleet-repair-3 found was real and is closed — but the repair replaced a direction twinning with a SYNTAX twinning, and the repair_log's stated ground for the new 1-in-3 is half false on the bytes.
findings.evidence: repair_log fleet-repair-3 and NOTES: ”A, C och D är tre likriktade angrepp på samma räkning … med identisk form och 8 ord var”. The word count is exact and this audit re-derived it (8/8/8/8, ratio 1.00). The form is not identical. A ”Den räknar MED för många armaturer i stolparna.” and D ”Den räknar MED fler timmar än beslutet gäller.” share one frame — räkna med plus a comparative-quantity phrase naming an input — while C ”Den räknar PÅ lampor som redan är utbytta.” uses a different one, räkna på plus a basis. B is odd again, on the verb (”Den bygger på”). The set is 1/2/1, not 1/3. A test-wise solver who strips B on category (the strip the floor already prices in) then has two formally parallel co-hyponyms differing only in which input they name, neither with any edge over the other, and the symmetric-pair elimination takes both — landing on C.
findings.why: Non-blocking and deliberately filed below F2. The symmetric-pair heuristic is second tier, well below the near-mechanical direction elimination that fleet-repair-3 removed, so the repair was a genuine net improvement rather than a wash; a plain solver does sit at 1-in-3. The empirical counterweight is strong here: G-STEM r3 returned a clean PASS on q:1 from the stems sheet, having found no blind path at all. What is worth the record is the justification, not the number: a floor stated on ”identisk form” that is not identical is a floor a later reader cannot re-derive. If the margin is ever wanted, the cheap edit is to move D onto C's frame (a basis claim rather than a quantity claim) so that no two options are twins.

findings.claim: The Q1 rationale contradicts itself between its A-clause and its D-clause, and separately over-claims uniformity across the four options in the sentence that carries its ”no option falls on direction alone” argument.
findings.evidence: The A-clause: ”men textens invändning gäller aldrig hur många armaturer som sitter uppe” — i.e. the fixture count is never disputed. The D-clause, four sentences later: ”Timantalet är det enda i kalkylen han aldrig bestrider.” Both cannot hold, and on the passage neither is the whole truth: at least three inputs go undisputed — the fixture count, the hour count, and the electricity price, which enters as reported fact (”Elnotan har stigit”) and is never contested. The second item: ”Samtliga fyra angriper dessutom kalkylen i samma riktning – de påstår att besparingen är för högt räknad”. B does not. ”Den bygger på en enda räkning av löpare” asserts a thin evidential basis, not an overstated figure — which the same rationale effectively concedes two sentences later when it argues that a headcount is not a line in the computation at all.
findings.why: Teaching payload, not answer design: no key moves, no distractor becomes defensible, and each individual argument against A, B and D is sound on its own. But the integrated read exists to catch exactly this — a rationale whose two halves disagree about which line items the author leaves alone, in the same breath as a universal claim that one of its own four options falsifies. Both are one-clause repairs: soften ”det enda” to ”den post D pekar ut bestämmer han aldrig” or similar, and narrow ”Samtliga fyra” to the three options it actually describes.

findings.stage_challenged: language / integrated (Q1 rationale, residue after fleet-repair-3b)
findings.claim: Two residues in the same rationale: ”räkning” does double duty across two senses in one payload, and the frame repetition G-SPRÅK r3 named is only half repaired.
findings.evidence: Polysemy: the rationale uses ”räkning” for the COMPUTATION — ”alla fyra optioner prövas mot samma räkning: den som ger 38 000 kronor om året” and ”annan post i samma räkning” — and for a HEADCOUNT — ”räkningen av löpare” and ”en räkning av personer”. The sentence that would disambiguate the two is precisely the broken one in F1. Frame repetition: G-SPRÅK r3 run 3 flagged ”ett uppblåst timantal skulle mycket riktigt blåsa upp besparingen” for two things, the uppblåst/blåsa-upp collocation AND the fact that ”the clause reuses the A-clause frame verbatim (”skulle mycket riktigt blåsa upp besparingen”)”. fleet-repair-3b varied the verb only — shipping reads ”skulle mycket riktigt förstora besparingen” against A's ”skulle mycket riktigt blåsa upp besparingen” — so ”skulle mycket riktigt” still stands verbatim in both clauses (count re-run by this audit: 2).
findings.why: Cosmetic, and recorded together with F1 because they share a sentence and a repair round. The polysemy is the more substantive of the two: the argument the student is asked to follow is that one kind of räkning is not an input to another kind of räkning, and it is made in a paragraph that uses the word for both without marking the shift, in a clause that does not parse. Repairing F1 with the gate's prescription (”en besparing räknad i kronor”) fixes the polysemy at the same time. The frame repetition is worth a second verb only if the sentence is being touched anyway.

findings.stage_challenged: language (CARRIED, UNRESOLVED — 3-of-3 unanimous, on a student-facing string)
findings.claim: The only STUDENT-FACING string flagged in G-SPRÅK round 3 was flagged by all three legs, and it was carried unrepaired with the unanimity not recorded.
findings.evidence: verdicts/verdicts-gsprak-r3.jsonl, re-read leg by leg: runs 1, 2 and 3 each flag ”Den räknar med fler timmar än beslutet gäller.” at minor, class 6 — ””gälla” followed by a quantity of hours reads first as a period of validity (biljetten gäller 60 minuter), not as the scope a decision covers, and the bare comparative clause wants ”vad”” — with the native alternative ”Den räknar med fler timmar än beslutet omfattar.” Every other r3 finding is confined to rationale prose. The only other 3-of-3 item was the fleet-repair-3 build identifier, which WAS repaired. repair_log fleet-repair-3b records this one as ”minors (”än beslutet gäller”, ”en poäng”) carried” — accurate as far as it goes, but it files a unanimous finding on an option beside a 1-of-3 finding on the passage without distinguishing them.
findings.why: The string is one of the eight the student reads, and it is a NEW string — fleet-repair-3 wrote it, so the flag is on the repair's own output rather than on inherited text. The prescribed fix is free: ”omfattar” for ”gäller” keeps the option at 8 words, keeps Q1's ratio at exactly 1.00, keeps the scope_shift trap identical (the decision is still two hours on its face), introduces no absolutizer and opens no cross-question bridge — verified: ”omfatta” shares no content lemma or 5-character stem with any Q2 option. There is precedent for re-taking exactly this kind of deferral: batches/batch17/audits/las-b17-003.json carried a 3-of-3 G-SPRÅK minor once, flagged that the evidence base had escalated, and the following ägardom re-took it and chose ÄNDRA. Worth the same treatment, at a cost of one word.

findings.claim: The proposal the passage ends on does not cover the year, in a text that is otherwise numerically exact.
findings.evidence: §5 concedes ”mellan maj och augusti kan spåret gott släckas tidigt” and demands ”håll tänt till elva från oktober till mars”; §4 puts the dark evening hours ”mellan oktober och mars”. April and September fall in neither bucket and are never assigned. The surrounding prose is precise to the hour, the day and the krona — klockan 21 mot 23, den 1 oktober, alla dagar i veckan, 38 000, två tredjedelar, tolv tusen — which is what makes the two unassigned months visible. Adjacent and milder: the opening scene is ”en onsdagskväll i november” while the closing ask is that the matter be taken at ”nämndens novembermöte” — internally possible (an early-November evening, a later meeting) but tight enough that a careful reader pauses.
findings.why: Cosmetic, and immaterial to both keys: Q2-B needs only ”sommaren” against ”vintertid”, and no option in the unit names a month. It is also arguably authentic — real insändare say summer and winter loosely. Recorded because the integrated read's remit is coherence a single-dimension gate cannot see, and because a debate piece whose entire case is that someone else's arithmetic does not survive scrutiny invites the reader to check its own.

findings.claim: Two accuracy items in the search log. One is arithmetic and errs in the safe direction; the other is a genuine RULE 14 coverage gap — the one-diacritic variant of the surname was never probed — which this audit closed.
findings.evidence: (a) The log states: ”Närmaste kända verkliga namn probat: ”Tjängvide” (Gotland) => 2 Nominatim-träffar; skiljer sig på två tecken från Tjernvide, alltså ej enbokstavsvariant.” Levenshtein(Tjernvide, Tjängvide) computed by this audit = 3, not 2 (ä/e, n/r, g/n). The conclusion holds a fortiori. (b) The log probes Tjängvide but never Tjärnvide. Levenshtein(Tjernvide, Tjärnvide) = 1 — a single diacritic — and tjärn is a productive Swedish toponymic element, which puts it squarely in the class RULE 14 names by example (”real ”Rössmåla” sits one diacritic from batch16's ”Rossmåla””). This audit ran it: sv.wiki exact ”Tjärnvide” 0, ”Folke Tjärnvide” 0, Nominatim se ”Tjärnvide” 0, against controls returning 56 and 10. Also added and clean: Bjässamon 0, Bjässemo 0, Bjässeberget 0, plus en.wikipedia and Wikidata as second indexes for both names, 0 on each with passing controls.
findings.why: The result is clean, so this is a method finding rather than a collision finding — the names stand. It is filed because the gap is exactly the one the rule was written to prevent after batch16 shipped Skarpbo and Rossmåla, and because the log presents its variant sweep (”variantprober ”Bässemon”, ”Bjessemon””) as if it were systematic when it varied only the toponym and not the surname. One further honest limit worth stating: RULE 14's Swedish recipe pairs sv.wiki with Nominatim, and Nominatim cannot speak to a PERSON name at all, so under the prescribed transport ”Folke Tjernvide” rests on one index. That is why this audit added two.

findings.claim: M-FORM in this worktree is running the PRE-ägardom absolutizer list, so the completion recorded as adopted in batch18's own binding addendum is not enforced — and the unit's hedge_map claims a check the tool could not have performed.
findings.evidence: BRIEF-ADDENDUM efterhandstillägg 2 (ägardom, bead hpf-y1p4) records the family as ”fullbordad” with nothing, nobody, ”no one”, ingenting, ingenstans and uteslutande added, and a bank-wide 0→0 before/after run over 114 units / 333 questions. gates/scripts/mech.py line 333, read directly: _ABSOLUTIZERS holds 25 tokens — alltid, aldrig, samtliga, alla, allt, varje, enbart, endast, ingen, inget, inga, helt, omöjligt, garanterat, always, never, every, all, only, none, entirely, impossible, proves, guarantees, certainly — and NONE of the six. A grep for ingenting, ingenstans, uteslutande and nobody across gates/ returns nothing but an unrelated 2026-07-30 eval-run note. The unit's NOTES nevertheless state that the option sets were checked ”mot M-FORM-familjen, inkl. de nya ingenting/ingenstans/uteslutande”. NOTES rule 13 repeats the completed list in full as if it were live.
findings.why: Immaterial to las-b18-002 and stated as such: this audit scanned the passage, both stems, all eight options and both rationales for all six tokens and found zero, so the unit would pass either list. It is filed at info as a batch-level state note — M-FORM is a weaker instrument than the record says for everything batch18 ran through it, and a generator NOTES claiming a check against a list the tool does not hold is the kind of drift that only surfaces when someone reads the source. Either mech.py is behind the ägardom in this worktree, or the ägardom landed elsewhere and never reached it.

findings.claim: The byline surname enters on an already-crowded stem. No rule is broken; the pool's narrowness is what is being recorded.
findings.evidence: The excluded full-name pairs already carry Birgitta Tjärnfeldt and Bodil Tjärnedal; Folke Tjernvide makes three surnames on the Tjärn-/Tjern- element in the bank. RULE 8's near-duplicate clause targets one-letter variants (the Quennerly/Quennerby near-pair under disposition); the nearest existing surname here sits at edit distance 5, well clear. ”Folke” is absent from the union of the 231 declared given names and batch17's 14 additions, verified by parsing the addendum rather than reading it, and no listed given name even starts fol-. ”Bjässemon” is absent from the toponym/street list at nearest distance 7.
findings.why: Recorded for the same reason batch19's G-REGISTER recorded ”Ödgren” entering on the heavily used -gren tail: no breach, but a visible sign that the naming generator draws from a narrow Swedish toponymic-surname pool, and the register gate is the place that tracking belongs. Nothing owed on this unit's account.

ship_recommendation: SHIP AFTER ONE ONE-CLAUSE FIX. No blocker survived the hunt: both keys are correct and uniquely licensed, no distractor is defensible, every quotation resolves, the arithmetic reconciles, mech is genuinely six of six on the shipping bytes, the sheets are exact leak-free projections, the rounds 2 and 3 repair tickets are byte-exact, and law 16 is clear with passing controls on four indexes. The one thing that should not ship as it stands is F1, because ”ingen post i en kronor i besparing” does not parse and sits in the Swedish explanation payload; the fix is the gate's own prescription, one clause, no effect on any option, stem, passage, key or length, and it repairs F5's polysemy at the same time. F6 is the next-cheapest and is worth taking on the batch17 precedent: one word, ”gäller” to ”omfattar”, on a student-facing option flagged unanimously by three native-review legs, with the length profile and the trap unchanged. Everything else is optional. F2 is the unit's principal residual and is recorded rather than repaired, in line with the adopted stance policy and the batch16 precedent — but the owner should know that the policy's tolerance is being drawn on a floor whose stated derivation this audit falsified, and that buying the margin back costs one option edit on Q2-C.
